sources.text: Trazodone is used to treat behavioral disorders, especially anxiety- or phobia-related in dogs, including separation anxiety, noise phobia such as fireworks or thunderstorms, veterinary visits, hospitalization, and travel. Several medications should be used with caution when given with trazodone, including SSRIs, MAO inhibitors, and CNS depressants. Trazodone should not be used in pets who are using MAO inhibitors or have angle-closure glaucoma.

Signs of serotonin syndrome in dogs include vomiting, diarrhea, seizures, elevated body temperature, increased skin sensitivity, depression, dilated pupils, vocalization, blindness, excessive drooling, difficulty breathing, incoordination, disorientation, and in severe cases coma or death. Signs typically develop within 1 to 12 hours of dosing.
